data.name: Bhawar
data.gender_notes: Bhawar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who holds the universe in the palm of his hand, the Lord of Time and Creator of the Universe. The name Bhawar carries the meaning “Lord of Time” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Bhawar usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of time and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine power and the creator of the universe, symbolizing wisdom, strength, and power
data.etymology: Bhawar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Time.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhawar total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_sanskrit.name: भवर
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit root 'bhau' meaning 'to be', 'to exist', 'to create', and the suffix 'ar' meaning 'one who', 'ruler of'. One who brings happiness into existence or creates happiness.

in_hindi.name: भवर
in_hindi.long_meaning: In Hindi, 'bhawar' can be translated as 'bhagya vadiya', meaning 'one who brings good fortune' or 'one who is blessed'.

in_tamil.name: பவர்
in_tamil.long_meaning: In Tamil, 'pavar' can mean 'lord' or 'master'. So, 'bhawar' could be interpreted as 'lord of happiness' or 'master of happiness'.

in_telugu.name: భవర్
in_telugu.long_meaning: In Telugu, 'bhawar' can be translated as 'bhogodheshapurojit', meaning 'one who rules over happiness' or 'one who is the lord of happiness'.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Bhawar' holds rich cultural significance as it is derived from the Sanskrit language, which is deeply rooted in Indian traditions and ancient Hindu philosophy. In Hindu mythology, Bhagavan Bhawar is revered as the supreme deity, the Lord of the Universe who governs time and creation. This name infuses a sense of reverence and acknowledgment of the divine power that governs the universe.
data.spiritual_significance: Bhawar, as a spiritual name, represents the divine power that holds the universe in its palm, the Creator of Time and the Source of All Existence. It is a reminder of the omnipresence and omniscience of God, symbolizing the unity and interconnectedness of all things in the cosmos. The name evokes a deep sense of divinity, piety, and devotion. It encourages one to remember the divine presence within themselves and to surrender to the will of God, embracing the spiritual journey towards enlightenment and self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bhawar signifies the one who is deeply absorbed in the bliss of the divine self (Bhava), constantly longing for union with the Supreme Consciousness.
